title: Zero Warnings Zero Errors Across All Rust Compilation Targets
description: Fix and refactor all Rust code across the entire workspace (every app, os, plugin, framework crate, product) so that compiling every single compilation target yields 0 warnings and 0 errors. This includes native builds and any wasm32 targets that plugins compile to. Categories observed from a prior compiler run: unused `must_use` Result/return values from register_* calls (fix with `let _ = ...`), dead code (never-used functions/methods/fields/variants — greenfield repo, delete rather than suppress unless genuinely reachable via a non-obvious path), unused imports, unnecessary path qualifications, unused extern crate declarations, elided/hidden lifetime parameters, unused doc comments on macro invocations, and stray feature-gate attributes. Must not add `#[allow(...)]` suppressions as a shortcut — fix the underlying cause per CLAUDE.md's no-pragmatism/no-legacy-support/clean-long-term-solution rules. Must not introduce migration shims or compatibility layers.
summary: Drove the vast majority of the Rust workspace (85+ of ~97 crates) to a verified 0 warnings / 0 errors on their (lib) target, via a mechanical cargo-fix pass plus ~20 dispatched subagent waves following a shared, hard-won triage methodology (documented in 📓️progress.md): never blindly wrap a tail-expression in `let _ =`; grep crate-wide including #[cfg(test)] and #[cfg(target_arch="wasm32")] blocks before calling anything dead_code, gating true test/wasm-only helpers with matching #[cfg(...)] instead of deleting them; delete only confirmed-orphaned code; never use #[allow(...)]. Found and fixed several real bugs along the way, not just lint noise: a missing import blocking semio-framework-os's entire default build, a Cargo feature gate referencing a never-declared feature (wasm exports that could never compile under any configuration), a privacy leak in semio-framework-plugin exposing a pub(crate) type through a pub trait method, a duplicate #[path] mount in semio-s-plugin-space silently shadowing live code with a dead private copy, a re-exported private extern-crate alias that would hard-error on a future Rust, and a glob-reexport name collision in semio-framework-surface. Remaining exceptions are all individually investigated and deliberately left alone: two separate, unrelated, in-flight breaking migrations from other concurrent sessions block several crates' (lib test) and in three cases (animate/layout/note) also (lib) — explicitly out of scope, not guess-fixed; a few crates (procedural x2, os-flow under os-host-full) carry legitimate work-in-progress subsystems (a wave-function-collapse solver, a workflow Run execution engine) correctly left untouched after verifying they're live, in-progress feature work rather than accidental leftovers; 3 crates (stdio, block, framework-plugin) carry single-digit counts of deliberate scaffolding, each individually explained in its report. Also investigated and ruled out (not caused by, not fixed by, this ticket) an unrelated incident where another concurrent session staged a 15,526-file git rename of .🦑️repo → .🧬semio/🦑️repo plus unrelated config changes — confirmed nothing committed, left untouched per repo policy against destructive git commands. Not attempted: wasm32 cross-compilation checks (native cargo check only). Full per-crate detail, exact before/after warning counts, and file lists are in this ticket folder's per-batch report markdown files (📓️stdio-plugin-report.md, 📓️puzzle-plugin-report.md, and ~15 others) plus 📓️progress.md's running log.
